title: Columbia dance, Charleston gun and the watermelon backdrop
summary: He tells of a dance in Columbia where the promoter ran off with the money, Willie forced to dance like Cab Calloway at gunpoint in Charleston, and watermelon backdrops.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: And then, of course... We were playing a Colored dance

in Columbia, South Carolina, with Willie Bryant, where we had to go at say 11 o'clock. So we said, "We're very sorry, we have to stop the dance" -- because the man ran away with the money. So what happens is the fellows come up...the people there, they waved to Willie and said, "Willie, you know, you've got that money. Why don't you give us a break? You took the money yourself." And Willie said, "No, honest! Honestly, the man ran off with the money." "Oh come on, man, play us another tune. You know you got the money."
Well, it's true. The guy came in, just took the bankroll from the band, and you know, he disappeared.

And another time in Charleston, South Carolina, Willie had to dance like Cab Calloway, because a guy held a 45 on him, and he says... Willie says, "I don't know nothin' about Cab Calloway," and the guy said, "Oh yes, you do. You're gonna dance like Cab Calloway." He pulled out this big 45...! So we saw Willie dancing, we wondered what the hell... [LAUGHS] The guy turned around and he said, "What's he doing?" He never saw Willie like this...
Well, of course, it's funny now, but it wasn't...
It wasn't too funny then, no. I mean, they would dress for a dance, because I mean, usually they'd have
a watermelon backdrop or something like that, you know... The watermelon wasn't so bad as a backdrop, but the one who was eatin' it...! [LAUGHS] That didn't go too good with the band!
